knowledge_statements.statement_title: Discrete entropically regularized multi-marginal transport
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the finite discrete EOT objective, its extended-value entropy, and the boundary convention at zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mu_i\), \(i\in[N]\), be discrete marginals on finite sets of cardinalities \(\ell_i\), let \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell_1\times\cdots\times\ell_N}\), and let \(\varepsilon>0\). The entropically regularized transport problem is
\[
\min_{\gamma\in\Pi(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_N)} F_\varepsilon[\gamma],\qquad F_\varepsilon[\gamma]=\langle C,\gamma\rangle+\varepsilon H(\gamma),
\]
where
\[
H(\gamma)=\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\sum_r\gamma_r(\log\gamma_r-1),&\gamma\geq0,\\
+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
The convention is \(0\log0=0\); consequently, the right derivative at zero of \(t\mapsto t(\log t-1)\) is \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finite discrete marginals, entropically regularized optimal transport minimizes transport cost plus epsilon times the extended negative entropy over the coupling set. The convention 0 log 0 = 0 is used, and the scalar entropy summand has right derivative minus infinity at zero.
assumptions_latex: \(N\) is a positive integer and each \(\mu_i\) is a discrete marginal on a finite set of cardinality \(\ell_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \min_{\gamma\in\Pi(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_N)}\{\langle C,\gamma\rangle+\varepsilon H(\gamma)\}\), where \(H(\gamma)=\sum_r\gamma_r(\log\gamma_r-1)\) for \(\gamma\geq0\), \(H(\gamma)=+\infty\) otherwise, and \(0\log0=0\).

children.title: Entropic Strict Convexification
children.top_down_role: Strict convexity induced in the regularized transport problem.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The entropically regularized transport objective is strictly convex on \(\Pi(a,b)\) and therefore has a unique minimizer.

notation.meaning: Relative entropy with the continuous extension at zero.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite balanced transport regularized relative to the positive product measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(C\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), define
\[F_\varepsilon(\pi)=\langle C,\pi\rangle+\varepsilon\,\mathrm{KL}(\pi\|r),\qquad \pi\in\Pi(a,b).\]
Because \(r_{ij}>0\) and the scalar entropy integrand is strictly convex, \(F_\varepsilon\) is strictly convex on every nontrivial segment in \(\Pi(a,b)\). Since the transportation polytope is compact and nonempty, the regularized problem has exactly one minimizer \(\pi^\varepsilon\). On positive entries, the entropy curvature is \(\varepsilon/\pi_{ij}>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding positive relative-entropy regularization makes the finite transport objective strictly convex on the feasible polytope, selecting a unique optimal coupling.
knowledge_statements.title: Entropic Strict Convexification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strict-convexity and uniqueness property is mathematically consistent for positive marginals and positive regularization, but no entropic-transport citation with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Coupling Smoothing
children.top_down_role: Diffusion of transport mass across coupling support.

assumptions_latex: \(\pi^\varepsilon\) minimizes the entropy-regularized balanced transport objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every entry satisfies \(\pi_{ij}^\varepsilon=a_i b_j\exp((f_i+g_j-C_{ij})/\varepsilon)>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gibbs representation and full support for finite positive marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exist dual potentials \(f\) and \(g\), unique up to \((f,g)\mapsto(f+t\mathbf1,g-t\mathbf1)\), such that
\[\pi_{ij}^\varepsilon=a_i b_j\exp\!\left(\frac{f_i+g_j-C_{ij}}{\varepsilon}\right).\]
Equivalently, \(\pi^\varepsilon=\operatorname{diag}(u)K\operatorname{diag}(v)\) for positive scaling vectors \(u,v\) chosen to enforce the marginals. Hence every finite-cost pair receives strictly positive mass, replacing the sparse support of an unregularized vertex by a smooth full-support coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The entropic optimizer is a diagonally scaled Gibbs kernel. With positive marginals and finite costs, every source-target pair receives positive mass.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupling Smoothing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Gibbs representation, gauge freedom, and full-support conclusion are internally consistent for finite costs and positive marginals, but they lack a supporting source with a specific locator.

children.title: Dual-Potential Smoothing
children.top_down_role: Regularity effects on dual potentials under entropic regularization.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Potential Smoothing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional log-sum-exp smoothing of the discrete dual transform.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each source index \(i\), the hard transform \(\min_j(C_{ij}-g_j)\) is replaced by \(T_{\varepsilon,i}(g)\). This function is concave and infinitely differentiable on \(\mathbb R^n\), with
\[\nabla T_{\varepsilon,i}(g)=-p_i(g),\qquad \nabla^2T_{\varepsilon,i}(g)=-\frac1\varepsilon\bigl(\operatorname{Diag}(p_i(g))-p_i(g)p_i(g)^{\mathsf T}\bigr).\]
Thus nondifferentiable selection among tied minimizers becomes Gibbs-weighted selection. The Hessian is negative semidefinite and annihilates \(\mathbf1\). Correspondingly, the transform is affine-equivariant under constant shifts: \(T_{\varepsilon,i}(g+t\mathbf1)=T_{\varepsilon,i}(g)-t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Entropy replaces the hard minimum over target potentials by a smooth log-sum-exp. Its gradient is a negative Gibbs assignment, its Hessian is a negative covariance, and constant potential shifts change the transform affinely.
assumptions_latex: All costs \(C_{ij}\) and potentials \(g_j\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The entropic transform is infinitely differentiable, with gradient \(-p_i(g)\) and Hessian \(-\varepsilon^{-1}(\operatorname{Diag}p_i-p_ip_i^{\mathsf T})\).

notation.meaning: Entropic soft minimum for source index i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual representation of entropically regularized discrete transport
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized dual-potential representation and the componentwise exponential correspondence between optimal potentials and transport scaling vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In the standing discrete entropic-transport setting,
\[
\mathrm L_{\mathbf C}^{\varepsilon}(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)=\max_{\mathbf f\in\mathbb R^n,\,\mathbf g\in\mathbb R^m}\left\{\langle\mathbf f,\mathbf a\rangle+\langle\mathbf g,\mathbf b\rangle-\varepsilon\left\langle e^{\mathbf f/\varepsilon},\mathbf K e^{\mathbf g/\varepsilon}\right\rangle\right\}.
\]
For optimal dual potentials \((\mathbf f,\mathbf g)\), the corresponding scaling vectors satisfy
\[
(\mathbf u,\mathbf v)=\left(e^{\mathbf f/\varepsilon},e^{\mathbf g/\varepsilon}\right),
\]
where exponentiation is componentwise.

Optimal potentials correspond to the transport scaling vectors through componentwise exponentiation by the inverse regularization parameter.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularized Wasserstein Cost and Its Self-Cost Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the transport cost evaluated at an entropically regularized optimal coupling and the explicitly normalized, self-cost-corrected divergence used to remove its nonzero diagonal bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varepsilon>0\). For discrete probability measures \(\alpha,\beta\) with weights \(\mathbf a,\mathbf b\), suppose \(C_{ij}=d(x_i,x_j)^p\), \(\mathbf P^\star\) solves the entropically regularized transport problem, and \((\mathbf f^\star,\mathbf g^\star)\) are corresponding dual solutions. Define \(\mathfrak P_{\mathbf C}^{\varepsilon}(\mathbf a,\mathbf b):=\langle\mathbf P^\star,\mathbf C\rangle=\left\langle e^{\mathbf f^\star/\varepsilon},(\mathbf K\odot\mathbf C)e^{\mathbf g^\star/\varepsilon}\right\rangle\) and \(\mathcal W_{p,\varepsilon}(\alpha,\beta)^p:=\mathfrak P_{\mathbf C}^{\varepsilon}(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)\). For general probability distributions, if \(\pi^\star\) is an entropically regularized optimal coupling, define \(\mathcal W_{p,\varepsilon}(\alpha,\beta)^p:=\int_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}d(x,y)^p\,\mathrm d\pi^\star(x,y)\). Because generally \(\mathcal W_{p,\varepsilon}(\alpha,\alpha)\neq0\), define \(\widetilde{\mathcal W}_{p,\varepsilon}(\alpha,\beta)^p:=2\mathcal W_{p,\varepsilon}(\alpha,\beta)^p-\mathcal W_{p,\varepsilon}(\alpha,\alpha)^p-\mathcal W_{p,\varepsilon}(\beta,\beta)^p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regularized Wasserstein cost is the ground transport cost evaluated at an entropically regularized optimal coupling. Its diagonal value generally does not vanish, so the corrected divergence subtracts both self-costs from twice the cross-cost.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sinkhorn Alternating Scaling Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded algorithm statement including the marginal equations, scaling gauge, and the extract's qualitative convergence assertion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\mathbf P=\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf u)\mathbf K\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf v)\), the marginal constraints are
\[\mathbf u\odot(\mathbf K\mathbf v)=\mathbf a,\qquad \mathbf v\odot(\mathbf K^\top\mathbf u)=\mathbf b.\]
Beginning with a positive \(\mathbf v^{(0)}\), with \(\mathbf v^{(0)}=\mathbb 1_m\) as the displayed initialization, Sinkhorn's iteration is
\[\mathbf u^{(\ell+1)}=\frac{\mathbf a}{\mathbf K\mathbf v^{(\ell)}},\qquad \mathbf v^{(\ell+1)}=\frac{\mathbf b}{\mathbf K^\top\mathbf u^{(\ell+1)}},\]
where division is componentwise. The scaling representation is invariant under \((\mathbf u,\mathbf v)\mapsto(\lambda\mathbf u,\mathbf v/\lambda)\) for \(\lambda>0\). Different positive initializations can yield different scaling representatives, but the iterations converge to representatives producing the same optimal coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sinkhorn's algorithm alternately rescales the kernel to impose its two prescribed marginals. The scaling vectors have a reciprocal scaling ambiguity, while the induced coupling is common at convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbf P=\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf u)\mathbf K\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf v)\) is in \(\mathbf U(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)\).
The componentwise quotients in the iteration are well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The alternating updates enforce the two marginal equations successively, and their induced couplings converge to the same optimal coupling despite the gauge freedom in \((\mathbf u,\mathbf v)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hilbert-Metric Convergence and Residual Bounds for Sinkhorn Iterates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded Sinkhorn convergence theorem using the strictly positive-kernel contraction setting inherited from its cited dependency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the positive-kernel contraction setting, the Sinkhorn scalings satisfy
\[(\mathbf u^{(\ell)},\mathbf v^{(\ell)})\to(\mathbf u^\star,\mathbf v^\star),\]
with
\[d_{\mathcal H}(\mathbf u^{(\ell)},\mathbf u^\star)=O(\lambda(\mathbf K)^{2\ell}),\qquad d_{\mathcal H}(\mathbf v^{(\ell)},\mathbf v^\star)=O(\lambda(\mathbf K)^{2\ell}).\]
For \(\mathbf P^{(\ell)}=\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf u^{(\ell)})\mathbf K\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf v^{(\ell)})\),
\[d_{\mathcal H}(\mathbf u^{(\ell)},\mathbf u^\star)\leq\frac{d_{\mathcal H}(\mathbf P^{(\ell)}\mathbb 1_m,\mathbf a)}{1-\lambda(\mathbf K)},\]
\[d_{\mathcal H}(\mathbf v^{(\ell)},\mathbf v^\star)\leq\frac{d_{\mathcal H}((\mathbf P^{(\ell)})^\top\mathbb 1_n,\mathbf b)}{1-\lambda(\mathbf K)}.\]
If \(\mathbf P^\star\) is the unique regularized optimal coupling, then
\[\|\log(\mathbf P^{(\ell)})-\log(\mathbf P^\star)\|_\infty\leq d_{\mathcal H}(\mathbf u^{(\ell)},\mathbf u^\star)+d_{\mathcal H}(\mathbf v^{(\ell)},\mathbf v^\star).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sinkhorn's scaling vectors converge geometrically in Hilbert's projective metric. Their errors are bounded by marginal residuals and control the entrywise logarithmic error of the induced coupling.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbf K\in\mathbb R_{+,*}^{n\times m}\) is in the positive-kernel setting of the preceding contraction theorem, with \(\lambda(\mathbf K)<1\).
\((\mathbf u^{(\ell)},\mathbf v^{(\ell)})\) are the Sinkhorn scaling iterates for marginals \((\mathbf a,�\mathbf b)\).
\(\mathbf P^\star\) is the unique solution of the regularized transport problem under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaling iterates converge at rate \(O(\lambda(\mathbf K)^{2\ell})\) in \(d_{\mathcal H}\), obey the displayed marginal-residual estimates, and satisfy the displayed logarithmic coupling-error bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Marginal-Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A computable summed-L1 feasibility certificate for nonnegative approximate transport plans.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the marginal-residual certificate by \[r(P)=\lVert P\mathbf 1-a\rVert_1+\lVert P^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1-b\rVert_1.\] Then \[r(P)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad P\in\Pi(a,b).\] For \(\delta\geq0\), call \(P\) \(\delta\)-marginal-feasible when \(r(P)\leq\delta\). Thus the computable inequality \(r(P)\leq\delta\) certifies that the sum of the two marginal L1 discrepancies is at most \(\delta\); it does not by itself certify objective-value accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The summed L1 row- and column-marginal residual is zero exactly for feasible couplings; bounding it by delta directly certifies approximate marginal feasibility but not objective accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(P\in\mathbb{R}_+^{m\times n}\), and \(a\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\) have equal total mass.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[r(P)=0\iff P\in\Pi(a,b),\qquad r(P)\leq\delta\iff P\text{ is }\delta\text{-marginal-feasible}.\]

notation.meaning: sum of the row- and column-marginal L1 residuals

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq \mathcal P_\varepsilon(P)-\mathcal D_\varepsilon(f,g)\leq\delta\) certifies \(\delta\)-optimality of \(P\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate for a feasible discrete entropic transport plan and arbitrary dual potentials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(U(a,b)=\{P\in\mathbb R_+^{m\times n}:P\mathbf1=a,\ P^\top\mathbf1=b\}\), \(\mathcal P_\varepsilon(P)=\langle C,P\rangle+\varepsilon\sum_{ij}P_{ij}(\log P_{ij}-1)\), and \(\mathcal D_\varepsilon(f,g)=\langle f,a\rangle+\langle g,b\rangle-\varepsilon\sum_{ij}\exp((f_i+g_j-C_{ij})/\varepsilon)\). For every \(P\in U(a,b)\) and \(f\in\mathbb R^m\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), weak duality gives \(\mathcal D_\varepsilon(f,g)\leq\mathcal P_\varepsilon^\star\leq\mathcal P_\varepsilon(P)\). Hence a computed gap at most \(\delta\) certifies that both displayed objectives are within \(\delta\) of the common optimum.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric iteration bound for strictly positive discrete kernels in projective distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v^t\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) be the scaling vector after \(t\) full row-and-column Sinkhorn iterations, and let \(v^\star\) denote the optimal scaling ray. If the induced scaling map is \(\tau\)-contractive in \(d_H\), then \(d_H(v^t,v^\star)\leq\tau^tD_0\), where \(D_0=d_H(v^0,v^\star)\). Therefore, for \(0<\delta<D_0\), the iteration count \(t\geq\lceil\log(D_0/\delta)/(-\log\tau)\rceil\) guarantees \(d_H(v^t,v^\star)\leq\delta\). The count treats one row update followed by one column update as one iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projective contraction by a factor τ yields a logarithmic iteration count in the inverse target error.
knowledge_statements.title: Sinkhorn Iteration Complexity

children.title: Per-Iteration Arithmetic Cost
children.top_down_role: Operation cost of a single scaling sweep.

assumptions_latex: Arithmetic operations and scalar elementary evaluations have unit cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One full row-and-column scaling iteration costs \(\Theta(mn)\) arithmetic operations and uses \(O(m+n)\) auxiliary storage.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense serial arithmetic model without materializing a new transport matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(u\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\) and \(v\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), a full Sinkhorn iteration computes one product \(Kv\), updates \(u=a\oslash(Kv)\), computes one product \(K^\top u\), and updates \(v=b\oslash(K^\top u)\), where \(\oslash\) denotes componentwise division. The two dense matrix-vector products require \(\Theta(mn)\) arithmetic operations; the componentwise updates require \(\Theta(m+n)\). Thus the full iteration costs \(\Theta(mn)\), with \(O(m+n)\) auxiliary storage when \(K\) is already stored.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a dense m-by-n kernel, two matrix-vector products dominate each full Sinkhorn iteration, giving Θ(mn) arithmetic cost.

children.title: Total Arithmetic Complexity
children.top_down_role: Aggregate computational work across all scaling iterations.

assumptions_latex: The scaling map contracts projective error by \(\tau\in[0,1)\), from initial error \(D_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The arithmetic cost for projective error \(\delta\) is \(O\!\left(mn\log(D_0/\delta)/(-\log\tau)\right)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense serial total cost obtained by composing iteration count and per-iteration cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\delta<D_0\), take \(T=\lceil\log(D_0/\delta)/(-\log\tau)\rceil\) full iterations. Multiplying this iteration count by the \(\Theta(mn)\) cost of each dense row-and-column scaling step gives total arithmetic work \(O(mnT)\), equivalently \(O\!\left(mn\log(D_0/\delta)/(-\log\tau)\right)\). If \(\tau\) is bounded uniformly away from \(1\), this reduces to \(O(mn\log(D_0/\delta))\). Kernel construction and storage are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total dense arithmetic work equals the per-iteration Θ(mn) cost times the geometric-convergence iteration count.
knowledge_statements.title: Total Arithmetic Complexity

children.title: Accuracy-Dependent Complexity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Complexity variation across residual, objective, or transport accuracy targets.

assumptions_latex: The dense Sinkhorn scaling map has contraction factor \(\tau\in[0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform contraction gives logarithmic accuracy dependence, while \(1-\tau=\Theta(\delta^p)\) gives \(O(\delta^{-p}\log(D_0/\delta))\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional regimes determined by how the contraction gap varies with requested accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The geometric bound is \(T(\delta)=O(\log(D_0/\delta)/(-\log\tau))\). If \(\tau\leq\bar\tau<1\) uniformly, then \(T(\delta)=O(\log(D_0/\delta))\). If instead \(\tau=\tau(\delta)\uparrow1\), then \(-\log\tau(\delta)\sim1-\tau(\delta)\). Consequently, a contraction gap satisfying \(1-\tau(\delta)=\Theta(\delta^p)\) for \(p>0\) yields \(T(\delta)=O(\delta^{-p}\log(D_0/\delta))\). Multiplication by \(\Theta(mn)\) gives the corresponding dense arithmetic regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accuracy dependence is logarithmic under uniform contraction and becomes polynomial-logarithmic when the contraction factor approaches one with the tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Accuracy-Dependent Complexity Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound kind fits the accuracy-regimes leaf, and the statement clearly makes the polynomial-logarithmic regime conditional on the scaling of the contraction gap. A specific source is still required for using this parameterized contraction regime as a Sinkhorn complexity statement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Log-domain form of alternating Sinkhorn updates for a finite entropic transport problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize finite \(\beta^0\in\mathbb R^n\). For \(t=0,1,\ldots\), update \(\alpha_i^{t+1}=\varepsilon\log a_i-\varepsilon\log\sum_j\exp((\beta_j^t-C_{ij})/\varepsilon)\) for every \(i\), then \(\beta_j^{t+1}=\varepsilon\log b_j-\varepsilon\log\sum_i\exp((\alpha_i^{t+1}-C_{ij})/\varepsilon)\) for every \(j\). Stop when a prescribed marginal-residual or primal–dual-gap test holds. Return the implicit plan \(P_{ij}=\exp((\alpha_i+\beta_j-C_{ij})/\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sinkhorn updates become additive updates of logarithmic potentials, avoiding direct storage of potentially overflowing or underflowing scaling factors.
knowledge_statements.title: Log-Domain Scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is correct for the log-domain-scaling leaf, and the additive updates, domains, stopping criterion class, and implicit output plan are stated consistently. No source or locator is provided for this stabilized Sinkhorn formulation.

children.title: Log-Sum-Exp Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Stable evaluation of exponential reductions in logarithmic coordinates.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\log\sum_k e^{x_k}=M+\log\sum_k e^{x_k-M}\), with every shifted exponent in \((0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Max-shifted representation used in finite log-domain Sinkhorn reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\in\mathbb R^N\), define \(\operatorname{LSE}(x)=\log\sum_{k=1}^N\exp(x_k)\). With \(M=\max_kx_k\), the exact identity \(\operatorname{LSE}(x)=M+\log\sum_{k=1}^N\exp(x_k-M)\) holds. Since \(x_k-M\leq0\) and at least one shifted value equals \(0\), all exponentials belong to \((0,1]\) and their sum belongs to \([1,N]\). This representation prevents exponential overflow and bounds the logarithm's argument away from zero in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting the maximum before exponentiation evaluates log-sum-exp exactly while keeping all exponential arguments nonpositive.
knowledge_statements.title: Log-Sum-Exp Evaluation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the log-sum-exp-evaluation leaf, and the exact max-shift identity and bounds are mathematically precise. Despite being standard, the record supplies neither an authoritative source nor a specific locator, as required by the review contract.

children.title: Shifted Exponential Accumulation
children.top_down_role: Dynamic-range control through shifted exponential evaluations.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The shifted sum \(S_s=\sum_ke^{x_k-s}\) is bounded by \(N\), and \(\sum_ke^{x_k}=e^sS_s\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rescaling identity and magnitude bounds for shifted exponential sums.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(S_s=\sum_{k=1}^N\exp(x_k-s)\). If \(s\geq\max_kx_k\), then \(0<S_s\leq N\) because every summand lies in \((0,1]\). The unshifted sum is recovered exactly as \(\sum_k\exp(x_k)=\exp(s)S_s\), while its logarithm is \(s+\log S_s\). Choosing \(s=\max_kx_k\) additionally gives \(1\leq S_s\leq N\), which avoids overflow during accumulation and ensures that at least one summand is represented as \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common upper shift bounds every exponential by one; choosing the maximum also keeps the accumulated sum between one and N.
knowledge_statements.title: Shifted Exponential Accumulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind is acceptable for the shifted-accumulation leaf, and the statement correctly distinguishes a general upper shift from the maximum shift. It lacks the required inspectable citation and locator.

children.title: Scaling-Factor Absorption
children.top_down_role: Transfer of accumulated scaling factors into stable potential representations.

assumptions_latex: \(K_{ij}=\exp(-C_{ij}/\varepsilon)>0\), with current potentials \(\alpha,\beta\) and residual scalings \(u,v>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absorbing \(u,v\) into \(\alpha,\beta\) leaves the represented transport plan unchanged.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact absorption identity for stabilized discrete Sinkhorn factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the current implicit plan is \(P_{ij}=u_i\exp((\alpha_i+\beta_j-C_{ij})/\varepsilon)v_j\). Define absorbed potentials \(\alpha_i'=\alpha_i+\varepsilon\log u_i\) and \(\beta_j'=\beta_j+\varepsilon\log v_j\), then reset \(u_i'=1\) and \(v_j'=1\). For every \(i,j\), \(u_i'\exp((\alpha_i'+\beta_j'-C_{ij})/\varepsilon)v_j'=P_{ij}\). Thus absorption changes only the numerical representation, not the plan, its marginals, or its objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding logarithms of residual scalings to the stored potentials and resetting those scalings to one preserves the transport plan exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Factor Absorption

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the scaling-factor-absorption leaf, and the absorption identity consistently preserves the represented plan. No authoritative stabilized-Sinkhorn source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Dual-Potential Recentering
children.top_down_role: Gauge shifts used to keep dual potentials within a stable numerical range.

assumptions_latex: The entropic plan is represented by potentials \(\alpha\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transformation \((\alpha,\beta)\mapsto(\alpha+c\mathbf1,\beta-c\mathbf1)\) preserves the plan and dual objective.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gauge recentering for balanced entropic transport dual potentials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(c\in\mathbb R\), set \(\alpha' =\alpha+c\mathbf1_m\) and \(\beta'=\beta-c\mathbf1_n\). Then \(\alpha_i'+\beta_j'=\alpha_i+\beta_j\), so every plan entry \(P_{ij}=\exp((\alpha_i+\beta_j-C_{ij})/\varepsilon)\) is unchanged. Moreover, the linear dual term changes by \(c\mathbf1^\top a-c\mathbf1^\top b=cM-cM=0\); hence the dual objective is invariant. The constant may therefore be chosen to center either potential vector without altering the represented optimization state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Opposite constant shifts of the two dual potentials preserve both the transport plan and balanced entropic dual objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Potential Recentering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the dual-potential-recentering leaf, and equal total masses suffice for invariance of both the plan and the displayed dual linear term. The claim nevertheless has no cited source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Absorption Trigger Regimes
children.top_down_role: Threshold regimes governing when stabilization is applied.

assumptions_latex: Residual scalings satisfy \(u\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\) and \(v\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absorption is triggered exactly when \(\max\{\|\log u\|_\infty,\|\log v\|_\infty\}\geq L\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold condition defining a generic stabilized-absorption regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(L>0\), define the safe residual-scaling region \(\mathcal S_L=\{(u,v):u>0,\ v>0,\ \|\log u\|_\infty<L,\ \|\log v\|_\infty<L\}\). Trigger absorption upon leaving \(\mathcal S_L\), equivalently when \(\max\{\|\log u\|_\infty,\|\log v\|_\infty\}\geq L\). The absorption update adds \(\varepsilon\log u\) and \(\varepsilon\log v\) to the stored potentials and resets the residual scalings to one. The value of \(L\) is selected from the floating-point exponent range and desired safety margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absorb residual scalings when either logarithmic scaling magnitude reaches a chosen numerical threshold; the threshold depends on the arithmetic format.
knowledge_statements.title: Absorption Trigger Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the absorption-trigger leaf, and the statement explicitly defines the trigger relative to a chosen threshold rather than presenting a universal numerical constant. Because this is an implementation-dependent stabilization policy, a specific algorithmic or numerical source is required.

children.title: Recentering Precision Limits
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision limitations affecting repeated potential shifts.

assumptions_latex: Floating-point arithmetic has unit roundoff \(u_{\rm mach}\).
Recentering forms \(x-c\) for finite floating-point numbers \(x,c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Recentering cannot recover information already lost, and subtraction may incur absolute error of order \(u_{\rm mach}(|x|+|c|)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision boundary of gauge recentering; exact invariance does not imply numerical reversibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the standard rounding model, a computed difference satisfies \(\operatorname{fl}(x-c)=(x-c)(1+\theta)\) with \(|\theta|\leq u_{\rm mach}\) when the operation is normal and no underflow or overflow occurs. Nevertheless, the input values may already carry absolute errors of order \(u_{\rm mach}|x|\) and \(u_{\rm mach}|c|\). Thus recentering very large, nearly equal potentials can leave uncertainty of order \(u_{\rm mach}(|x|+|c|)\), overwhelming a small true difference. Gauge shifts preserve the exact plan but cannot restore digits previously lost through rounded updates, exponentiation, underflow, or overflow.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact gauge invariance has a precision limit: subtracting large nearby potentials cannot recover digits already lost to floating-point rounding.
knowledge_statements.title: Recentering Precision Limits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind correctly fits the precision-limits leaf, and the statement distinguishes exact gauge invariance from loss of previously rounded information. The floating-point error model and absolute-error estimate require an authoritative numerical-analysis source with a specific section or theorem locator.

children.title: Regularization Continuation
children.top_down_role: Solution of a sequence of progressively sharper regularized problems.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularization Continuation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite discrete entropic transport with a decreasing regularization schedule and log-domain Sinkhorn solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose tolerances \(\tau_0,\ldots,\tau_L>0\) and finite initial potentials \((f^{(0)}_0,g^{(0)}_0)\), commonly \((0,0)\). For each \(l=0,\ldots,L\), apply stabilized log-domain Sinkhorn updates at regularization \(\varepsilon_l\), starting from \((f^{(l)}_0,g^{(l)}_0)\), until both marginal residuals are at most \(\tau_l\); denote the result by \((f^{(l)},g^{(l)})\). If \(l<L\), set \((f^{(l+1)}_0,g^{(l+1)}_0)=(f^{(l)},g^{(l)})\), modulo the gauge transformation \((f,g)\mapsto(f+c\mathbf 1,g-c\mathbf 1)\). Output the final coupling formed at \(\varepsilon_L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a sequence of increasingly less regularized transport problems, initializing each stabilized Sinkhorn solve with the preceding dual potentials, and return the coupling at the final regularization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi^{(L)}=\operatorname{diag}(e^{f^{(L)}/\varepsilon_L})e^{-C/\varepsilon_L}\operatorname{diag}(e^{g^{(L)}/\varepsilon_L})\) approximates the transport plan at the target regularization \(\varepsilon_L\) to the prescribed stopping tolerance.

notation.meaning: Entropic kernel at regularization level l

children.title: Dual-Potential Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reuse of dual potentials across nearby transport problems.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Potential Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Log-coupling fitting transfer of dual potentials between two positive regularization parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \((f',g')\) at \(\varepsilon'\), define \(s_{ij}=(f'_i+g'_j-C_{ij})/\varepsilon'\). At the new parameter \(\varepsilon\), compute warm-start potentials by solving \[\min_{f\in\mathbb R^m,\,g\in\mathbb R^n}\sum_{i,j}w_{ij}\left((f_i+g_j-C_{ij})/\varepsilon-s_{ij}\right)^2\] subject to one gauge constraint, and use a minimizer \((f^0,g^0)\) to initialize stabilized Sinkhorn. The old coupling is preserved exactly before further updates if and only if the minimum residual is zero. When \(\varepsilon\ne\varepsilon'\), this requires the relevant cost correction to admit an additive row-column decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer the old dual state by fitting its induced log-coupling at the new regularization. Exact preservation occurs only when the fitted residual is zero, equivalently when the required cost correction is row-column separable for distinct regularization parameters.
assumptions_latex: \(a\) and \(b\) are strictly positive probability vectors and \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) is finite.
Finite dual potentials \((f',g')\) have been computed at \(\varepsilon'>0\), and the next parameter is \(\varepsilon>0\).
The fitting weights satisfy \(w_{ij}>0\), and one gauge constraint is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The initialization satisfies \(e^{(f_i^0+g_j^0-C_{ij})/\varepsilon}=e^{(f'_i+g'_j-C_{ij})/\varepsilon'}\) for every \((i,j)\) if and only if the fitted residual is zero.

notation.meaning: Weights in the additive log-coupling fit

children.title: Coupling Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reuse of coupling information across successive solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupling Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Log-least-squares conversion of a positive previous coupling into Sinkhorn scaling factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \((x,y)\) as a minimizer of \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^m,\,y\in\mathbb R^n}\sum_{i,j}w_{ij}\bigl(x_i+y_j-\log(\widehat\pi_{ij}/K_{ij})\bigr)^2\] subject to a gauge such as \(x_1=0\). Set \(u_i^0=e^{x_i}\), \(v_j^0=e^{y_j}\), and initialize Sinkhorn with \(\pi^0=\operatorname{diag}(u^0)K\operatorname{diag}(v^0)\). Thereafter alternate the usual marginal scalings until the prescribed residual tolerance is met. If \(\widehat\pi=\operatorname{diag}(\widehat u)K\operatorname{diag}(\widehat v)\), the fit has zero residual and recovers an equivalent scaling pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fit row and column log-scalings so the new kernel-scaled coupling is as close as possible to a previous positive coupling, then start Sinkhorn from those factors.
assumptions_latex: \(K=e^{-C/\varepsilon}\) has strictly positive entries and \(\widehat\pi\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^{m\times n}\) is a previous coupling.
Weights \(w_{ij}>0\) and a gauge constraint are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The initialized vectors \(u^0=e^x\) and \(v^0=e^y\) minimize the selected weighted squared log-distance from \(\operatorname{diag}(u)K\operatorname{diag}(v)\) to \(\widehat\pi\).

children.title: Warm-Start Transfer Failures
children.top_down_role: Loss of initialization value after large parameter or support changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Transfer Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic obstruction to exact warm-start transfer across regularization levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose row indices \(i,k\) and column indices \(j,\ell\) satisfy \(\Delta=C_{ij}+C_{k\ell}-C_{i\ell}-C_{kj}\ne0\). For an entropic optimizer, the coupling cross-ratio obeys \[\log\frac{\pi_{ij}^{\varepsilon}\pi_{k\ell}^{\varepsilon}}{\pi_{i\ell}^{\varepsilon}\pi_{kj}^{\varepsilon}}=-\frac{\Delta}{\varepsilon}.\] Row-column rescaling leaves this cross-ratio invariant. Hence a coupling optimal at \(\varepsilon'\) cannot be converted into the optimizer at \(\varepsilon\ne\varepsilon'\) solely by changing row and column scaling factors. The absolute difference between the two log-cross-ratios is \(|\Delta|\,|1/\varepsilon-1/\varepsilon'|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero cost cross-difference makes optimal coupling cross-ratios depend on regularization. Because diagonal rescaling preserves cross-ratios, exact transfer between distinct regularization levels fails.
assumptions_latex: \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has a nonzero cost cross-difference on some two-by-two submatrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No row-column rescaling of the old optimal coupling can reproduce the new regularized optimizer when the displayed cross-difference is nonzero.

notation.meaning: Cost cross-difference on a two-by-two submatrix

knowledge_statements.title: Small-Regularization Ill-Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential conditioning mechanism for an explicitly formed Gibbs kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_{\min}=\min_{i,j}C_{ij}\) and \(C_{\max}=\max_{i,j}C_{ij}\). Then \[\frac{\max_{i,j}(K_\varepsilon)_{ij}}{\min_{i,j}(K_\varepsilon)_{ij}}=\exp\!\left(\frac{C_{\max}-C_{\min}}{\varepsilon}\right).\] Thus, whenever \(C_{\max}>C_{\min}\), the ratio diverges exponentially as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Multiplications by \(K_\varepsilon\), marginal divisions, and scaling vectors may consequently involve exponentially separated magnitudes even though the regularized optimization problem remains mathematically well-defined. This is conditioning of the kernel representation, not nonexistence of the exact entropic optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: As regularization decreases, the ratio between the largest and smallest Gibbs-kernel entries grows exponentially with the cost range, making direct Sinkhorn scaling increasingly ill-conditioned.
assumptions_latex: \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) is finite and has at least two distinct entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The kernel dynamic range is \(\exp((C_{\max}-C_{\min})/\varepsilon)\), which diverges as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).

children.title: Kernel Underflow
children.top_down_role: Loss of small kernel entries in finite-precision arithmetic.

assumptions_latex: Floating-point arithmetic rounds every positive real below \(x_{\min}>0\) to zero.
The kernel is formed as \(K_{ij}=e^{-(C_{ij}-c)/\varepsilon}\), where \(C_{ij}\ge c\) and \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{ij}-c>\varepsilon\log(1/x_{\min})\) implies that the stored kernel entry is zero.

notation.meaning: Smallest representable positive number under the chosen rounding convention

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entrywise underflow boundary for an explicitly exponentiated entropic kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any entry \((i,j)\), exact arithmetic gives \(K_{ij}>0\). In the stated floating-point model, the stored value is zero whenever \[e^{-(C_{ij}-c)/\varepsilon}<x_{\min},\quad\text{equivalently}\quad C_{ij}-c>\varepsilon\log(1/x_{\min}).\] At equality the result depends on rounding and whether subnormal numbers are retained. Such numerical zeros alter the kernel support and can make subsequent scaling infeasible even though the exact kernel is strictly positive. Choosing \(c=\min_{i,j}C_{ij}\) prevents overflow of the kernel but does not remove this underflow boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicitly computed Gibbs-kernel entry becomes numerical zero when its shifted cost divided by regularization exceeds the logarithmic positive-number range of the floating-point format.
knowledge_statements.title: Kernel Underflow

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The entrywise underflow boundary is mathematically coherent and the failure-boundary kind fits, but its floating-point model and threshold have no inspectable numerical-analysis citation.

children.title: Scaling-Factor Overflow
children.top_down_role: Numerical saturation of multiplicative scaling factors.

assumptions_latex: The largest finite floating-point number is \(x_{\max}\).
A direct Sinkhorn row update is \(u_i=a_i/(Kv)_i\), with \(a_i>0\), \(v\ge0\), and \((Kv)_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \((Kv)_i<a_i/x_{\max}\), the exact update exceeds \(x_{\max}\) and cannot be stored finitely.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Overflow boundary for direct multiplicative Sinkhorn scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The exact row update satisfies \(u_i=a_i/(Kv)_i\). It lies outside the finite floating-point range precisely when \[\frac{a_i}{(Kv)_i}>x_{\max},\quad\text{equivalently}\quad (Kv)_i<\frac{a_i}{x_{\max}}.\] A zero computed denominator yields an infinite or undefined update. The analogous column boundary is \((K^{\mathsf T}u)_j<b_j/x_{\max}\). Because the representation is gauge-invariant under \((u,v)\mapsto(\lambda u,v/\lambda)\), individual overflow may sometimes be postponed by rebalancing, but simultaneous excessive ranges require log-domain absorption or greater precision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direct Sinkhorn scaling factor overflows when its kernel-vector denominator is smaller than the target marginal divided by the largest finite representable number.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Factor Overflow

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The direct-update overflow inequality is correct under the stated model and fits the failure-boundary leaf, but no authoritative source or locator is provided.

children.title: Dynamic-Range Exhaustion
children.top_down_role: Insufficient representable range for simultaneous kernel and scaling values.

assumptions_latex: The usable positive floating-point interval is \([x_{\min},x_{\max}]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the required spread of any represented factor exceeds \(R=x_{\max}/x_{\min}\), no gauge keeps all its entries within the usable interval.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representability boundary after accounting for the global scaling gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a positive vector \(z\), some scalar multiple \(\lambda z\) lies componentwise in \([x_{\min},x_{\max}]\) if and only if \[\frac{\max_i z_i}{\min_i z_i}\le R.\] Consequently, the gauge transformation \((u,v)\mapsto(\lambda u,v/\lambda)\) cannot make a scaling vector representable when its intrinsic component ratio exceeds \(R\). Likewise, explicit storage of a positive kernel fails when \(\max K_{ij}/\min K_{ij}>R\). Crossing either boundary forces underflow, overflow, or loss of relative resolution in direct arithmetic, motivating log-domain stabilization or higher precision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gauge rescaling cannot rescue a kernel or scaling vector whose intrinsic largest-to-smallest ratio exceeds the usable floating-point dynamic range.
knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic-Range Exhaustion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The gauge-invariant component-ratio criterion is mathematically sound and appropriately classified, but the numerical representability claim lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Precision-Dependent Stability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Stability regimes determined by arithmetic precision.

knowledge_statements.title: Precision-Dependent Stability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Format-dependent threshold for storing every explicitly shifted Gibbs-kernel entry as positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After shifting by \(C_{\min}\), define \(K_{ij}=\exp(-(C_{ij}-C_{\min})/\varepsilon)\). Its largest entry is \(1\), and its smallest entry is \(\exp(-\Delta_C/\varepsilon)\). Therefore every exact kernel entry is at least \(x_{\min}\) only if \[\exp(-\Delta_C/\varepsilon)\ge x_{\min},\quad\text{equivalently}\quad \varepsilon\ge\frac{\Delta_C}{\log(1/x_{\min})}.\] Strict inequality gives margin against endpoint rounding; equality depends on the format and rounding convention. Log-domain Sinkhorn avoids explicit positive storage of all kernel entries but remains subject to finite-precision effects in log-sum-exp reductions and residual evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed cost range, the smallest regularization permitting every explicitly shifted kernel entry to remain positive is determined by the smallest usable positive floating-point number.
assumptions_latex: The number \(1\) is representable and positive values below \(x_{\min}>0\) are unusable or rounded to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive storage of every explicitly shifted kernel entry requires \(\varepsilon\ge\Delta_C/\log(1/x_{\min})\), up to endpoint-rounding conventions.

children.title: Structural Support Zeros
children.top_down_role: Kernel zeros imposed by forbidden or absent transport edges.

knowledge_statements.title: Structural Support Zeros
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact support zeros induced by forbidden transport edges, distinct from floating-point underflow.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A structural support zero is an entry \((i,j)\) excluded from the admissible transport graph \(E\). Representing exclusion by \(C_{ij}=+\infty\) gives \(K_{ij}=e^{-C_{ij}/\varepsilon}=0\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\), while \(K_{ij}>0\) for \((i,j)\in E\) when allowed costs are finite. Every admissible coupling must satisfy \(\pi_{ij}=0\) outside \(E\). These zeros are part of the mathematical model and persist in exact arithmetic; they must not be conflated with positive kernel entries rounded to zero by finite precision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structural zeros are exact forbidden transport edges, usually encoded by infinite cost. They constrain every admissible coupling and differ from positive kernel entries lost through numerical underflow.
assumptions_latex: The Gibbs kernel uses the convention \(e^{-\infty}=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_{ij}=0\) exactly on forbidden edges \((i,j)\notin E\), independently of numerical precision.

children.title: Scaling Infeasibility
children.top_down_role: Marginal constraints incompatible with the admissible support.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hall-type mass-deficiency certificate for support-constrained transport feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any row subset \(I\), all mass \(a(I)\) must be transported into its neighbor set \(N(I)\), whose prescribed receiving mass is \(b(N(I))\). Hence \[a(I)>b(N(I))\] is a verifiable certificate of infeasibility: no nonnegative matrix \(\pi\) supported on \(E\) can satisfy \(\pi\mathbf 1=a\) and \(\pi^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1=b\). Consequently, no diagonal scaling of a kernel supported on \(E\) can attain those marginals. A column-subset certificate is obtained by interchanging rows and columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If some set of rows contains more prescribed mass than all its allowed neighboring columns can receive, no supported coupling or exact kernel scaling can realize the marginals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A subset \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) with \(a(I)>b(N(I))\) certifies that no coupling with marginals \((a,b)\) can be supported on \(E\).

notation.meaning: Total source mass in a row subset
Columns adjacent to a row subset
Total target mass in the neighboring columns

children.title: Near-Infeasible Scaling
children.top_down_role: Ill-conditioned scaling near the boundary of support feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Infeasible Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative proximity to a Hall-type support-feasibility boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the nontrivial row Hall slack by \[\eta=\min_{\substack{\varnothing\ne I\subsetneq\{1,\ldots,m\}\\N(I)\ne\{1,\ldots,n\}}}\bigl(b(N(I))-a(I)\bigr),\] with \(\eta=+\infty\) if the indexing family is empty. Feasibility implies \(\eta\ge0\). For a prescribed application-dependent tolerance \(\tau>0\), call the instance \(\tau\)-near-infeasible when \(0\le\eta\le\tau\); the analogous column slack may also be evaluated. Small slack identifies proximity to a support-feasibility inequality but does not by itself imply a universal Sinkhorn iteration bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible scaling instance is called near-infeasible at tolerance tau when a nontrivial Hall mass inequality has slack between zero and tau; this does not alone determine an iteration count.
assumptions_latex: \(a\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and \(b\in\mathbb R_+^n\) are probability vectors, and \(E\) admits at least one coupling with these marginals.
Only nonempty proper row subsets \(I\) with \(N(I)\ne\{1,\ldots,n\}\) enter the displayed row-slack definition.
The tolerance \(\tau>0\) is chosen for the application.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The support-marginal pair is \(\tau\)-near-infeasible under this definition when \(0\le\eta\le\tau\).

notation.meaning: Minimum nontrivial row Hall slack over the displayed indexing family
Neighbor set in the allowed support graph

children.title: Support-Feasibility Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Structural checks connecting admissible support to prescribed marginals.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists P\in\mathbb R_+^{m\times n}:\ P\mathbf 1=r,\ P^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1=c,\ \operatorname{supp}(P)\subseteq S\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \forall I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\},\ \sum_{i\in I}r_i\leq\sum_{j\in N(I)}c_j.\]

notation.meaning: Neighbors of a row set in the support graph

review_flags: No supplied locator addresses transport-support feasibility; an optimal-transport or matrix-scaling source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite discrete support feasibility via the capacitated Hall condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form the bipartite graph whose allowed edges are \(S\). A coupling with marginals \(r,c\) and no mass outside \(S\) exists exactly when every row subset satisfies the displayed capacitated Hall inequality. Consequently, any subset \(I\) for which \(\sum_{i\in I}r_i>\sum_{j\in N(I)}c_j\) is a finite, directly verifiable certificate of scaling infeasibility. If all inequalities hold, a feasible coupling is obtainable as a maximum flow of value \(\sum_i r_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support feasibility is equivalent to every row subset having enough neighboring column capacity; a violating subset certifies that Sinkhorn scaling cannot attain the requested marginals.
knowledge_statements.title: Support-Feasibility Diagnostics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite capacitated Hall condition and infeasibility certificate fit this diagnostic leaf and are mathematically plausible, but no cited source or inspectable locator supports them.

assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb R_{++}^{m\times n}\) and \(r,c\) are strictly positive with equal total mass.
The current scaling vectors satisfy \(u\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\) and \(v\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration exactly enforces one selected marginal while leaving the other scaling vector unchanged.
review_flags: No supplied locator supports Greenkhorn; a computational optimal-transport source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact greedy single-coordinate scaling for a positive kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize positive \(u,v\). At an iteration compute \(a=P\mathbf1\) and \(b=P^{\mathsf T}\mathbf1\), then choose a row or column attaining \(\max\{\rho(a_i,r_i),\rho(b_j,c_j)\}\). If row \(i\) is selected, set \(u_i\leftarrow u_i r_i/a_i\); if column \(j\) is selected, set \(v_j\leftarrow v_j c_j/b_j\). Stop when \(\lVert a-r\rVert_1+\lVert b-c\rVert_1\leq\varepsilon\), and output \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greenkhorn selects the most violated row or column, rescales that single coordinate exactly, and stops when total marginal error meets tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Greedy Coordinate Scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf and the coordinate update is coherently specified, but the Greenkhorn selection score and update rule lack a supporting citation.

children.title: Greenkhorn Convergence Rates
children.top_down_role: Accuracy decay under greedy coordinate scaling.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable and coordinate-smooth with constants \(L_k>0\).
On the relevant level set, \(\lVert\nabla F(x)\rVert_2^2\geq2\mu(F(x)-F_*)\) for some \(\mu>0\).
At step \(t\), coordinate \(k_t\) maximizes \((\partial_kF(x_t))^2/L_k\) and is minimized exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F(x_t)-F_*\leq\left(1-\frac{\mu}{\sum_{k=1}^dL_k}\right)^t\bigl(F(x_0)-F_*\bigr).\]

notation.meaning: Polyak–Łojasiewicz constant on the level set

review_flags: Rate is an abstract coordinate-descent formulation; a source matching the Greenkhorn dual hypotheses is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear objective convergence under coordinate smoothness and a level-set PL inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For exact greedy coordinate minimization of the entropic transport dual, coordinate smoothness gives a one-step decrease of at least \((\partial_{k_t}F(x_t))^2/(2L_{k_t})\). The normalized greedy choice and the level-set Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality therefore yield the displayed geometric bound. The statement applies only while the stated constants are valid on the entire initial level set; it does not assert uniform global strong convexity of the unconstrained transport dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under coordinate smoothness and a level-set PL inequality, normalized greedy Greenkhorn decreases the dual objective geometrically.
knowledge_statements.title: Greenkhorn Convergence Rates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role is appropriate, but the record supplies only an abstract coordinate-descent PL rate and does not source or establish its applicability to the Greenkhorn dual.

children.title: Greenkhorn Iteration Complexity
children.top_down_role: Coordinate-update counts required for target accuracy.

assumptions_latex: The hypotheses and notation of the stated Greenkhorn convergence-rate bound hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[T\geq\frac{\sum_{k=1}^dL_k}{\mu}\log\!\left(\frac{F(x_0)-F_*}{\varepsilon}\right)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad F(x_T)-F_*\leq\varepsilon.\]
review_flags: Iteration bound depends on an abstract PL regime; a Greenkhorn-specific source and parameter translation are required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-coordinate iteration count for objective accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\kappa_G=(\sum_{k=1}^dL_k)/\mu\). Since \((1-1/\kappa_G)^T\leq\exp(-T/\kappa_G)\), the displayed number of exact greedy coordinate updates is sufficient for dual-objective error at most \(\varepsilon\). This count treats one row or column rescaling as one iteration and excludes initialization, marginal construction, coordinate selection, and rounding to an exactly feasible transport plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The PL-rate regime requires at most condition-number times log initial-error over target-error single-coordinate updates.
knowledge_statements.title: Greenkhorn Iteration Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The iteration-complexity kind fits the leaf, but the bound inherits an unsourced Greenkhorn-specific PL regime and parameter translation.

children.title: Greenkhorn Arithmetic Complexity
children.top_down_role: Total computational work including coordinate maintenance.

knowledge_statements.title: Greenkhorn Arithmetic Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense-kernel arithmetic bound with full score scanning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Multiplying the single-coordinate iteration bound by the assumed \(O(m+n)\) implementation cost gives the displayed arithmetic complexity. The bound counts scalar additions, multiplications, divisions, logarithms, and comparisons as constant-cost operations. It excludes the \(O(mn)\) storage and initialization cost, numerical-precision effects, and any final rounding procedure. Alternative heaps, lazy scores, sparsity, or implicit kernels change the per-iteration factor and are outside this model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a dense kernel and full score scans, arithmetic cost equals the iteration bound times a linear row-plus-column factor.
assumptions_latex: The dense \(m\times n\) kernel is explicitly stored.
A coordinate update, affected marginal update, and full score scan use \(O(m+n)\) arithmetic operations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The arithmetic complexity is \(O\!\left((m+n)\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{m+n}L_k}{\mu}\log\!\frac{F(x_0)-F_*}{\varepsilon}\right)\), and it suffices to ensure \(F(x_T)-F_*\leq\varepsilon\).
review_flags: TeX delimiters repaired; a source establishing Greenkhorn-specific constants and the stated cost model is still required.

children.title: Sinkhorn Comparison Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem regimes favoring greedy updates or full scaling sweeps.

assumptions_latex: Sinkhorn contracts its error by \(q_S\in(0,1)\) per full sweep costing \(C_S\) operations.
Greenkhorn contracts its error by \(q_G\in(0,1)\) per coordinate update costing \(C_G\) operations.
Both methods start from error \(E_0\) and target \(0<\varepsilon<E_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Greenkhorn has the smaller geometric-model cost exactly when \[\frac{C_G}{-\log q_G}<\frac{C_S}{-\log q_S},\] up to integer-rounding of iteration counts.
review_flags: This regime comparison is model-based; empirical and theorem-specific Greenkhorn–Sinkhorn sources are required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-normalized comparison under geometric error models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the stated geometric models, the respective costs to reach \(\varepsilon\) are approximately \(C_S\log(E_0/\varepsilon)/(-\log q_S)\) and \(C_G\log(E_0/\varepsilon)/(-\log q_G)\). Thus the displayed inequality defines the Greenkhorn-favorable regime. For dense square problems one commonly has a full Sinkhorn sweep costing order \(n^2\) and a maintained Greenkhorn coordinate update costing order \(n\), but the contraction factors may differ substantially.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greenkhorn is favored when its operation cost per unit logarithmic error contraction is smaller than Sinkhorn’s.
knowledge_statements.title: Sinkhorn Comparison Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits a comparison-regime leaf, and the cost-normalized inequality follows from the assumed geometric models, but no source supports those models or their relevance to Sinkhorn and Greenkhorn.

children.title: Batch Greenkhorn Variants
children.top_down_role: Greedy scaling variants that update coordinate blocks.

assumptions_latex: A nonempty batch contains coordinates from only one marginal side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every selected coordinate has its prescribed marginal immediately after the simultaneous same-side update.
review_flags: No supplied source identifies a canonical batch Greenkhorn variant or its convergence conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous exact rescaling of a same-side coordinate batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize positive \(u,v\). Select a batch \(B\) of \(s\) rows with largest row-violation scores and simultaneously set \(u_i\leftarrow u_i r_i/a_i\) for every \(i\in B\); alternatively select columns and set \(v_j\leftarrow v_j c_j/b_j\). Recompute affected marginals and repeat, allowing the side and batch size to vary. Stop when \(\lVert a-r\rVert_1+\lVert b-c\rVert_1\leq\varepsilon\), and output \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Batch Greenkhorn simultaneously rescales several highly violated coordinates from one marginal side, then refreshes affected marginal data.
knowledge_statements.title: Batch Greenkhorn Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and same-side batch update fit the leaf, but no citation identifies this as a recognized Batch Greenkhorn variant or states applicable convergence conditions.

children.title: Randomized Greenkhorn Variants
children.top_down_role: Coordinate scaling driven by randomized selection.

assumptions_latex: \(K,r,c,u,v\) are positive and define current marginal sums \(a,b\).
Sampling weights \(w_k\geq0\) have positive sum whenever the stopping test fails.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected coordinate is sampled from \(\Pr(k)=w_k/\sum_\ell w_\ell\) and is then scaled exactly to its target.
review_flags: Variant is mathematically specified, but no supplied locator supports its convergence or canonical attribution.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random coordinate selection biased by exact marginal violations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At each iteration set row weights \(w_i=\rho(a_i,r_i)\) and column weights \(w_{m+j}=\rho(b_j,c_j)\). Sample one coordinate proportionally to these weights. For a sampled row \(i\), apply \(u_i\leftarrow u_i r_i/a_i\); for a sampled column \(j\), apply \(v_j\leftarrow v_j c_j/b_j\). Stop using an exact marginal-error test, not a sampled estimate, and output the resulting scaled matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomized Greenkhorn samples a coordinate with probability proportional to its exact violation score and rescales that coordinate exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Greenkhorn Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The randomized coordinate rule is mathematically specified and fits the leaf, but its canonical attribution and convergence behavior have no cited support.

children.title: Stochastic Greenkhorn Variants
children.top_down_role: Scaling based on stochastic estimates or sampled information.

assumptions_latex: Unbiased positive estimators \(\widehat a_i,\widehat b_j\) of selected marginal sums are available.
Safeguards satisfy \(0<\ell\leq r_i/\widehat a_i,c_j/\widehat b_j\leq U<\infty\) after clipping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stochastic update preserves positivity and becomes exact coordinate scaling when \(\eta_t=1\) and the marginal estimate is exact.
review_flags: Stochastic Greenkhorn has multiple incompatible formulations; no supplied source selects convergence, noise, or step-size hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Damped coordinate scaling from stochastic marginal estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Sample a coordinate and estimate its current marginal from a minibatch or stochastic kernel oracle. For row \(i\), set \(q_t=\operatorname{clip}(r_i/\widehat a_i,\ell,U)\) and update \(u_i\leftarrow u_i q_t^{\eta_t}\); for column \(j\), analogously update \(v_j\leftarrow v_j\operatorname{clip}(c_j/\widehat b_j,\ell,U)^{\eta_t}\). Periodically compute exact marginal error for stopping, and output the last positively scaled matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stochastic Greenkhorn uses noisy marginal estimates with damping and clipping, while exact checks determine termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Greenkhorn Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source selects this stochastic formulation or its noise and step-size assumptions. Moreover, recovery of exact coordinate scaling also requires the exact ratio to remain unchanged by clipping.

children.title: Hybrid Coordinate-Update Variants
children.top_down_role: Combinations of greedy, batched, randomized, or stochastic selection.

assumptions_latex: Each available update rule preserves positivity of \(u,v\).
An exact marginal-error check is performed at prescribed checkpoints.
The scheduling policy chooses only finitely delayed eligible update rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The hybrid procedure returns a positive scaled matrix once the exact marginal-error tolerance is met.
review_flags: No supplied source establishes a standard hybrid schedule or convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scheduled mixtures of greedy, batch, randomized, and stochastic updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a rule from \(\mathcal R\) at each iteration using a fixed schedule or a state-dependent policy. Apply its greedy, batch, randomized, or stochastic scaling update, then refresh exactly or estimate the affected marginal state as required by the next rule. At each checkpoint compute \(E\); stop and output \(P=\operatorname{diag}(u)K\operatorname{diag}(v)\) when \(E\leq\varepsilon\). The rule schedule and checkpoint frequency are part of the algorithm specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid method schedules several coordinate-scaling rules but terminates only after an exact marginal-feasibility check.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Coordinate-Update Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the hybrid-variant leaf, but positivity and finite scheduling delay do not establish attainment of the stopping tolerance, and no source supports a standard hybrid schedule or convergence result.

children.title: Greedy Coordinate Selection
children.top_down_role: Priority rules for choosing marginal coordinates to rescale.

assumptions_latex: Current row and column sums \(a,b\) and positive targets \(r,c\) are available.
All candidate coordinates are eligible for update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[k_t\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}\left(\{\rho(a_i,r_i):1\leq i\leq m\}\cup\{\rho(b_j,c_j):1\leq j\leq n\}\right).\]
review_flags: No supplied locator supports the Greenkhorn score formula or its exact-improvement interpretation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum exact-improvement selection among row and column coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive \(x,y\), the score \(\rho(x,y)\) is nonnegative and vanishes exactly when \(x=y\). Compute the score of every current row and column marginal and select any maximizer as displayed. Exact rescaling of that coordinate decreases the entropic scaling dual by precisely its score under the usual dual normalization. A deterministic tie-breaking rule may be fixed without changing the selection criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a row or column maximizing the nonnegative scalar score equal to its exact coordinate-rescaling improvement.
knowledge_statements.title: Greedy Coordinate Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The greedy selection algorithm fits the leaf, but the score formula and its claimed equality with exact dual improvement require a Greenkhorn-specific source and normalization.

children.title: Violation-Score Maintenance
children.top_down_role: Maintenance of coordinate priorities or marginal violation scores.

assumptions_latex: \(P=\operatorname{diag}(u)K\operatorname{diag}(v)\) is represented by positive scalings and accessible kernel entries.
Current marginal sums and all violation scores are stored.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After each coordinate rescaling, the stated rank-one marginal correction produces the exact new marginal sums and hence exact refreshed scores.
review_flags: No supplied source supports the bookkeeping complexity or data-structure variants.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact incremental maintenance after one row or column scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Before scaling row \(i\) by \(q=r_i/a_i\), retain its entries \(P_{ij}\). Set \(a_i\leftarrow r_i\) and, for every column \(j\), set \(b_j\leftarrow b_j+(q-1)P_{ij}\); refresh the changed column scores and the selected row score. The column case is symmetric: set \(b_j\leftarrow c_j\) and \(a_i\leftarrow a_i+(q-1)P_{ij}\) for every row \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After one scaling, update the opposite marginals by the changed row or column entries and refresh only affected violation scores.
knowledge_statements.title: Violation-Score Maintenance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rank-one marginal corrections are plausible and fit the bookkeeping leaf, but the column case should explicitly set \(q=c_j/b_j\), and no source supports the bookkeeping or complexity claims.

children.title: Marginal-State Bookkeeping
children.top_down_role: Storage and refresh of quantities used by coordinate updates.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r=P\mathbf 1_m\) and \(c=P^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1_n\) remain exact after every coordinate update.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense-kernel bookkeeping for one-coordinate Greenkhorn updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(r=u\odot(Kv)\) and \(c=v\odot(K^{\mathsf T}u)\). If row multiplier \(u_i\) changes by \(\Delta u_i\), set \(r_i\leftarrow r_i+\Delta u_i(Kv)_i\) and, for every \(j\), set \(c_j\leftarrow c_j+v_jK_{ij}\Delta u_i\); other row entries remain unchanged. If column multiplier \(v_j\) changes by \(\Delta v_j\), set \(c_j\leftarrow c_j+\Delta v_j(K^{\mathsf T}u)_j\) and, for every \(i\), set \(r_i\leftarrow r_i+u_iK_{ij}\Delta v_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store both marginals and update them exactly in linear time after each row or column multiplier change.
knowledge_statements.title: Marginal-State Bookkeeping

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the bookkeeping leaf and the update identities are mathematically plausible, but no cited source supports this exact incremental-maintenance scheme.

children.title: Bookkeeping-Dominated Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where selection maintenance outweighs scaling work.

assumptions_latex: \(K\) is stored as a dense \(n\times m\) matrix
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bookkeeping cost is \(O(nm+T(n+m))\) time and \(O(n+m)\) auxiliary memory.

notation.meaning: Stored row and column marginal vectors

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic complexity for dense Greenkhorn state maintenance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Computing the initial marginal state \((r,c)\) requires \(O(nm)\) arithmetic operations. A row-coordinate update changes all \(m\) stored column marginals and costs \(O(m)\); a column-coordinate update changes all \(n\) stored row marginals and costs \(O(n)\). Hence any sequence of \(T\) updates costs at most \(O(nm+T(n+m))\) time and \(O(n+m)\) auxiliary storage. The regime is bookkeeping-dominated when multiplier computation is cheaper than updating or scanning these stored marginal and violation vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a dense kernel, maintaining and scanning marginal states can dominate the scalar scaling update itself.
knowledge_statements.title: Bookkeeping-Dominated Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the regime leaf, but the initialization, per-update, scanning, and auxiliary-memory claims have no inspectable transport-algorithm citation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multi-marginal Sinkhorn scaling representation and updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the multiplicative Gibbs representation of the unique discrete EOT optimizer and the cyclic marginal-rescaling update; the extract supplies no convergence guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite discrete EOT problem, the unique optimizer has the scaling form
\[
\gamma^{\star,\varepsilon}_r=\xi(r)\prod_{k=1}^{N}a_k(r_k)
\]
for suitable vectors \(a_k\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell_k}\). The cyclic scaling update is
\[
a_k^{(n+1)}(x)=\frac{\mu_k(x)}{\displaystyle\sum_{r:r_k=x}\xi(r)\prod_{i<k}a_i^{(n+1)}(r_i)\prod_{i>k}a_i^{(n)}(r_i)},\qquad x\in X_k,
\]
whenever the displayed denominator is nonzero. No convergence rate or convergence theorem is asserted here.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unique discrete entropically regularized transport optimizer is the Gibbs tensor multiplied by one scaling factor for each marginal. The multi-marginal Sinkhorn iteration cyclically replaces each factor by the target marginal divided by the marginal induced by the Gibbs tensor and the other factors, using newly updated earlier factors and previous-iterate later factors. The extract does not state a convergence guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The finite discrete EOT setup has \(\varepsilon>0\), finite cost entries, and a nonempty coupling set \(\Pi(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_N)\).
Each denominator appearing in the scaling update is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist vectors \(a_k\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell_k}\) such that \(\displaystyle\gamma^{\star,\varepsilon}_r=\xi(r)\prod_{k=1}^{N}a_k(r_k)\), and the factors may be updated cyclically by the stated marginal-normalization formula.
