children.title: Creation–Destruction Cycling
children.top_down_role: Redundant alternation between mass production and removal.

assumptions_latex: Creation and destruction have linear coefficients \(\alpha_+\) and \(\alpha_-\).
The model permits simultaneous equal creation and destruction at a fixed location.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Negative cycle cost \(\alpha_++\alpha_-<0\) makes the variational value unbounded below.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary negative-cycle calculation for linear mass penalties
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to additive linear penalties permitting simultaneous source cancellation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Add to any feasible path a colocated source pair with equal total masses \(M\ge0\): one creates \(M\) and the other destroys \(M\). Their net contribution to the continuity equation is zero, so the state path and endpoints are unchanged, while the action changes by
\[
M(\alpha_++\alpha_-).
\]
If \(\alpha_++\alpha_-<0\), sending \(M\to\infty\) drives the action to \(-\infty\). If \(\alpha_++\alpha_-=0\), arbitrarily large zero-cost cycles remain, destroying coercivity even though they do not lower the value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simultaneous create-destroy loop leaves the state unchanged; negative combined penalty makes the objective unbounded below, while zero combined penalty permits noncoercive free cycling.
knowledge_statements.title: Creation–Destruction Cycling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The negative-cycle calculation is valid only if arbitrary simultaneous colocated creation and destruction are admissible and the full action changes exactly by the stated linear term. Those model-specific facts and the coercivity conclusion require a source.

children.title: Penalty-Balance Stability Boundary
children.top_down_role: Transition between meaningful transport and degenerate mass variation.

assumptions_latex: Mass variation is penalized additively and linearly by coefficients \(\alpha_+\) and \(\alpha_-\).
Equal colocated creation and destruction are admissible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The no-negative-cycle condition is \(\alpha_++\alpha_-\ge0\), with strict stability at \(\alpha_++\alpha_->0\).

notation.meaning: Penalty paid by one unit creation-destruction cycle

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact cycle-cost balance for additive linear penalties
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cycle stability condition, distinct from positivity needed for metric separation in each direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an additive linear mass-variation action, the penalty balance preventing negative creation-destruction cycles is
\[
\alpha_++\alpha_-\ge0.
\]
Strict inequality makes every nonzero equal-mass cycle costly and supplies coercivity in the cycled mass. Equality is the boundary: cycles are cost-neutral and minimizing sequences may carry unbounded source variation. If the value is also required to separate measures directionally, the stronger individual conditions \(\alpha_+>0\) and \(\alpha_->0\) are necessary in this model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative combined creation and destruction penalty prevents negative cycles; strict positivity suppresses free cycling, while positive individual penalties are needed for directional separation.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Balance Stability Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sum condition controls the specified cycling direction, but strict positivity alone does not establish global coercivity or stability of an otherwise unspecified action. A source and a complete model definition are required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Schrödinger Bridge Path-Space Formulation and Entropic Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Path-space KL formulation, its discrete Brownian-bridge representation, induced interpolation, small-noise limit, and regularized dynamic representation in the stated setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\overline{\mathcal K}_\varepsilon\) denote the Brownian reference law on path space. The Schrödinger bridge is the unique solution
\[
\bar\pi_\varepsilon^\star=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\bar\pi\in\overline{\mathcal U}(\alpha_0,\alpha_1)}\operatorname{KL}(\bar\pi\mid\overline{\mathcal K}_\varepsilon).
\]
As \(\varepsilon\to0\), this solution converges to a solution of the classical path-space optimal-transport problem. For discrete endpoint measures, if
\[
\pi_\varepsilon^\star=\sum_{i,j}P_{\varepsilon,ij}^\star\delta_{(x_i,y_j)},
\]
then
\[
\bar\pi_\varepsilon^\star=\sum_{i,j}P_{\varepsilon,ij}^\star\bar\gamma_{x_i,y_j}^\varepsilon,
\qquad
\alpha_{\varepsilon,t}=P_{t\sharp}\bar\pi_\varepsilon^\star
=\sum_{i,j}P_{\varepsilon,ij}^\star\mathcal G_{t(1-t)\varepsilon^2}\!\left(\cdot-\gamma_{x_i,y_j}(t)\right).
\]
The same entropic interpolation is represented by minimizing
\[
\int_0^1\!\int_{\mathbb R^d}\left(\lVert v_t(x)\rVert^2+\frac{\varepsilon}{4}\lVert\nabla\log\alpha_t(x)\rVert^2\right)d\alpha_t(x)\,dt
\]
over curves satisfying the continuity equation and prescribed endpoint conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Schrödinger bridge is the unique KL projection of a Brownian path law onto path laws with prescribed endpoint marginals. Its time marginals define entropic interpolation; for discrete measures they are Gaussian-blurred mixtures of geodesic trajectories. In the stated small-noise limit the bridge approaches classical path-space optimal transport, and the interpolation also has a kinetic-energy-plus-Fisher-information formulation.
assumptions_latex: \overline{\mathcal K}_\varepsilon\text{ is the stated Brownian reference path law}
(\alpha_t,v_t)\text{ satisfies the continuity equation and prescribed endpoint conditions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar\pi_\varepsilon^\star=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\bar\pi\in\overline{\mathcal U}(\alpha_0,\alpha_1)}\operatorname{KL}(\bar\pi\mid\overline{\mathcal K}_\varepsilon),\qquad \alpha_{\varepsilon,t}=P_{t\sharp}\bar\pi_\varepsilon^\star,\qquad \bar\pi_\varepsilon^\star\text{ converges to a classical path-space OT solution as }\varepsilon\to0

assumptions_latex: \(R\) is a probability measure on path space over a Polish state space, with endpoint law \(R_{01}\).
Endpoint laws \(\mu_0,\mu_1\) are prescribed and the entropy constraint set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dynamic Schrödinger entropy infimum equals the static endpoint-coupling entropy infimum.

auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint-constrained Schrödinger bridge relative to a fixed reference path law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X_0,X_1\) be the endpoint maps. Then
\[
\inf_{\substack{P\in\mathcal P(\Omega)\\(X_0)_\#P=\mu_0,\ (X_1)_\#P=\mu_1}}H(P\mid R)
=
\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu_0,\mu_1)}H(\pi\mid R_{01}).
\]
Indeed, the entropy chain rule separates endpoint entropy from conditional-path entropy. For any feasible endpoint coupling \(\pi\), the least conditional contribution is zero and is attained by mixing the reference bridges \(R^{xy}\): \(P=\int R^{xy}\,d\pi(x,y)\). Thus an optimal static coupling, when it exists, determines a dynamic Schrödinger bridge with reference conditional dynamics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Schrödinger bridge entropy minimization over path laws reduces to relative-entropy minimization over endpoint couplings; optimal paths retain the reference process conditioned on their endpoints.
knowledge_statements.title: Static Entropy-Minimization Representation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The static–dynamic entropy identity is standard but requires a standard-Borel path space, measurable endpoint maps, disintegration hypotheses, and careful treatment of infinite entropy. No supporting citation is supplied, and the statement includes proof-style justification.

assumptions_latex: \(R^\varepsilon\) is Brownian law with initial marginal \(\mu_0\) and diffusivity \(\varepsilon>0\)
Admissible controls are progressively measurable and have finite kinetic energy
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\inf_{P:\,P_0=\mu_0,\,P_1=\mu_1}H(P\mid R^\varepsilon)=\inf_u\frac{1}{2\varepsilon}\mathbb E\!\left[\int_0^1\lVert u_t\rVert^2\,dt\right].\]

notation.meaning: Brownian reference path law of diffusivity epsilon

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Brownian-reference formulation with fixed initial and terminal marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R^\varepsilon\) be the law on \(C([0,1];\mathbb R^d)\) of \(dX_t=\sqrt{\varepsilon}\,dW_t\), with \(X_0\sim\mu_0\). Among path laws \(P\ll R^\varepsilon\) satisfying \(P_0=\mu_0\) and \(P_1=\mu_1\), the Schrödinger bridge minimizes relative entropy. By the drift representation of finite-entropy changes of Brownian measure, this problem is equivalently
\[\inf_{P:\,P_0=\mu_0,\,P_1=\mu_1}H(P\mid R^\varepsilon)=\inf_u\frac{1}{2\varepsilon}\mathbb E\!\left[\int_0^1\lVert u_t\rVert^2\,dt\right],\]
where the second infimum is over weak controlled diffusions \(dX_t=u_t\,dt+\sqrt{\varepsilon}\,dW_t\) having the prescribed endpoint laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Schrödinger bridge equals a minimum-energy stochastic control problem whose controlled diffusion connects the prescribed endpoint distributions.

assumptions_latex: \(R\) is a Markov path law with time marginals \(m_t\)
The Schrödinger bridge exists and has endpoint-factor form \(dP^*/dR=f(X_0)g(X_1)\)
\(f,g\) are nonnegative and normalized so that \(P^*\) is a probability law
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mu_t=(f_tg_t)m_t,\qquad f_t(x)=\mathbb E_R[f(X_0)\mid X_t=x],\quad g_t(x)=\mathbb E_R[g(X_1)\mid X_t=x].\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marginal flow induced by a Markov Schrödinger bridge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P^*\) be the Schrödinger bridge relative to a Markov reference law \(R\), and suppose \(dP^*/dR=f(X_0)g(X_1)\). For \(0\le t\le1\), define
\[f_t(x)=\mathbb E_R[f(X_0)\mid X_t=x],\qquad g_t(x)=\mathbb E_R[g(X_1)\mid X_t=x].\]
If \(m_t=R_t\), then the time marginal \(\mu_t=P_t^*\) satisfies
\[\frac{d\mu_t}{dm_t}(x)=f_t(x)g_t(x).\]
The curve \((\mu_t)_{t\in[0,1]}\), with \(\mu_0\) and \(\mu_1\) as endpoints, is the entropic interpolation associated with \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An entropic interpolation is the marginal flow of the optimal bridge; each density factors into forward and backward Schrödinger potentials.
knowledge_statements.title: Entropic Interpolation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The marginal-factor representation matches entropic interpolation, but the endpoint-factor form and conditional-potential formula have no cited source with a specific locator.

children.title: Schrödinger Factor System
children.top_down_role: Coupled potential or factor representation underlying Schrödinger bridges.

knowledge_statements.title: Schrödinger Factor System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-marginal factor equations for a strictly positive reference kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \((Kh)(x)=\int_X k(x,y)h(y)\,m(dy)\) and \((K^*h)(y)=\int_X k(x,y)h(x)\,m(dx)\). A pair of positive measurable functions \((f,g)\) solves the Schrödinger factor system for endpoint densities \((\rho_0,\rho_1)\) when
\[f(x)(Kg)(x)=\rho_0(x)\quad m\text{-a.e.},\qquad g(y)(K^*f)(y)=\rho_1(y)\quad m\text{-a.e.}\]
Then \(d\pi(x,y)=f(x)k(x,y)g(y)\,m(dx)m(dy)\) has marginals \(\rho_0m\) and \(\rho_1m\). The factors are invariant under \((f,g)\mapsto(cf,c^{-1}g)\) for \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Schrödinger factors rescale a positive reference kernel so that the resulting coupling has the prescribed two marginals.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_0,\rho_1\) are probability densities with respect to \(m\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f\,Kg=\rho_0,\qquad g\,K^*f=\rho_1.\]

children.title: Iterative Proportional Fitting
children.top_down_role: Alternating marginal scaling for Schrödinger bridge computation.

assumptions_latex: The kernel operator \(K\) maps positive functions to strictly positive functions

notation.meaning: positive kernel operator and its adjoint
coupling after a complete scaling cycle

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternating multiplicative scaling for the two-marginal Schrödinger system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(g^{(0)}>0\), perform alternating pointwise updates
\[f^{(n+1)}(x)=\frac{\rho_0(x)}{(Kg^{(n)})(x)},\qquad g^{(n+1)}(y)=\frac{\rho_1(y)}{(K^*f^{(n+1)})(y)}.\]
After a complete cycle, form
\[d\pi^{(n+1)}(x,y)=f^{(n+1)}(x)k(x,y)g^{(n+1)}(y)\,m(dx)m(dy).\]
Each half-step enforces one prescribed marginal while retaining the multiplicative kernel form. Stop when both marginal residuals satisfy a chosen tolerance, and output the current coupling or scaling factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: IPFP alternately rescales the kernel coupling to enforce the first and second marginals, stopping when both marginal residuals are small.
knowledge_statements.title: Iterative Proportional Fitting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The alternating updates correctly serve the IPFP algorithm container and make no unsupported convergence assertion, but no source with a specific locator supports the continuous-kernel formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(P^{(0)}=R\). Given \(P^{(n)}\), impose the initial marginal and then the terminal marginal by
\[\frac{dP^{(n+1/2)}}{dP^{(n)}}=\frac{d\mu_0}{dP^{(n)}_0}(X_0),\qquad \frac{dP^{(n+1)}}{dP^{(n+1/2)}}=\frac{d\mu_1}{dP^{(n+1/2)}_1}(X_1).\]
Each multiplier depends only on one endpoint, so every iterate remains an endpoint scaling of \(R\). Stop when discrepancies between \(P^{(n)}_0,P^{(n)}_1\) and \(\mu_0,\mu_1\) meet the prescribed tolerance; output \(P^{(n)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Path-space scaling alternately multiplies the current path law by initial- and terminal-state density ratios to impose the endpoint laws.
knowledge_statements.title: Path-Space Scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and endpoint-density updates match path-space scaling, but their validity and preservation of endpoint-scaling form require an inspectable authoritative citation.

assumptions_latex: There exist constants \(0<m\le M<\infty\) with \(m\le k(x,y)\le M\) almost everywhere
The target densities are strictly positive
Scaling iterates remain in the positive cone
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_H(Ku,Kv)\le q\,d_H(u,v),\qquad q\le\tanh\!\left(\frac12\log\frac{M}{m}\right)<1.\]

notation.meaning: Hilbert projective distance on positive functions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniformly positive bounded-kernel regime for projective stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For positive functions, let \(d_H(u,v)=\log(\operatorname*{ess\,sup}u/v)-\log(\operatorname*{ess\,inf}u/v)\). If \(m\le k(x,y)\le M\) almost everywhere, then the positive integral operator \(K\) has finite projective diameter and satisfies
\[d_H(Ku,Kv)\le q\,d_H(u,v),\qquad q\le\tanh\!\left(\frac12\log\frac{M}{m}\right)<1.\]
Pointwise multiplication and division by a fixed positive density preserve projective distance. Consequently, a full Schrödinger scaling cycle is contractive projectively, giving uniqueness of the scaling factors up to reciprocal constants and geometric stability of normalized iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniformly positive bounded kernel makes Schrödinger scaling contractive in Hilbert projective distance, yielding uniqueness and geometric stability after normalization.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Stability Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the stability-regime container, but the exact Birkhoff contraction bound and the resulting uniqueness and geometric-stability conclusions need a source establishing all required positivity, existence, and projective-metric hypotheses.

assumptions_latex: \(F_\varepsilon\) is restricted to couplings of \(\mu_0\) and \(\mu_1\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\min_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu_0,\mu_1)}F_\varepsilon(\pi)\longrightarrow\frac12W_2^2(\mu_0,\mu_1),\qquad \varepsilon\downarrow0.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic entropic transport limit in Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\varepsilon>0\), define on \(\mathcal P(\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d)\)
\[F_\varepsilon(\pi)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle \frac12\int\lVert x-y\rVert^2\,d\pi+\varepsilon H(\pi\mid\mu_0\otimes\mu_1),&\pi\in\Pi(\mu_0,\mu_1),\\+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]
As \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), the functionals \(F_\varepsilon\) Gamma-converge, for weak convergence together with uniform second-moment control, to the unregularized quadratic transport functional. Hence
\[\min F_\varepsilon\longrightarrow\frac12W_2^2(\mu_0,\mu_1),\]
and every weak accumulation point of entropic minimizers is an optimal quadratic transport plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: As entropic noise vanishes, regularized quadratic transport costs converge to Wasserstein cost, and accumulation points of minimizers are optimal transport plans.
knowledge_statements.title: Small-Noise Transport Limit

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits the small-noise limit container, but no citation supports the stated Gamma-convergence topology, convergence of minima, and accumulation-point conclusion. The phrase “weak convergence together with uniform second-moment control” also requires authoritative clarification as an equicoercivity or topology condition.
